# ethereum-optimism/ecosystem Weekly Report (May 17 - 23, 2026)

## 🚀 Highlights
This week focused primarily on protocol maintenance, test suite optimization, and the refinement of migration strategies for the Superchain. Developers prioritized triaging the backlog, identifying several outdated issues and potential duplicates related to `OPContractsManagerMigrator` and `op-chain-ops`. Significant technical discussion centered on resolving flaky end-to-end tests and determining the most efficient path for migrating dispute game tests to improve long-term stability.

## 🛠️ Key Developments
While no new features or code refactors were merged during this period, the groundwork was laid for several infrastructure improvements:

### Test Suite & Infrastructure Planning
*   **Dispute Game Test Migration:** Developers evaluated strategies for moving dispute game tests from `op-e2e/super_test.go` to `op-acceptance-tests` ([#20814](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/20814)). A notable proposal emerged to integrate `op-supernode` into `op-e2e` as a more efficient alternative to using `op-supervisor`, potentially accelerating the migration process.
*   **Interoperability Documentation:** The team determined that specific interop transaction pool eviction behaviors during reorgs are now sufficiently handled within `op-reth`, leading to a decision that additional standalone documentation for this specific behavior is no longer required ([#19351](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/19351)).

## 🐛 Issues & Triage
The week saw a concerted effort to clean up the repository and diagnose persistent testing bottlenecks.

### Closed Issues
*   **Outdated Logic & Duplicates:** Several issues were closed as they were superseded by protocol changes. This included a command issue in `op-chain-ops` ([#17470](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/17470)) rendered obsolete by the removal of the `superRootsActive()` branch, and a mocking issue ([#17928](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/17928)) now covered by real migration tests.
*   **Spam Mitigation:** A spam issue generated by an AI agent was identified and promptly closed ([#20847](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/20847)).

### Active & New Issues
*   **Flaky Test Investigation:** Significant effort is being directed toward `TestELSyncSafeRetractedByOffset` ([#20334](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/20334)). Analysis suggests a configuration conflict where a 10-second offset is installed before a baseline sync gate, creating an unreachable equality target and causing 72-second timeouts. Proposed next steps include logging the delta between the sequencer and verifier safe heads to confirm if the offset is blocking the gate.
*   **Migration Tooling Redundancy:** Potential duplicates were flagged regarding the `OPContractsManagerMigrator` ([#20502](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/20502)) and the creation of a `superchain-ops` template ([#20503](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/20503)), indicating an ongoing effort to streamline the development of Superchain deployment tools.

## 💬 Community & Collaboration
Collaboration this week was characterized by deep technical troubleshooting and architectural debate. The discussion surrounding issue [#20814](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/20814) showcased active problem-solving regarding the trade-offs between different testing frameworks (`op-supernode` vs. `op-supervisor`). Furthermore, the rapid identification and closure of AI-generated spam and duplicate issues demonstrate a high level of maintainer vigilance in keeping the project's scope focused and its backlog manageable.
